source.title: Geometry-Adaptive Explainer for Faithful Dictionary-Based Interpretability under Distribution Shift
source.authors: Sung-Jun Lim; Heedong Kim; A. Lee; Kyungwoo Song

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether interpretations attributed to the same selected SAE feature IDs persist across decoder adaptations. It reports substantial but incomplete retention and explicitly cautions that unchanged feature activations do not guarantee unchanged semantics or causal effects; it does not test superposition itself.
record.gate_note: The paper tests dictionary-explainer alignment and adaptation under distribution shift, not whether sparse features overlap to fit limited dimensions, why neurons are polysemantic, or whether LLM features are distributed across neurons. GAE-versus-baseline faithfulness metrics and geometric-gap measurements are not rows for those versions. Rows below are limited to reported feature-attribution and concept-retention results bearing on V5.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs and transcoders as tools and mainly reports how its own decoder-adaptation method (GAE) performs against other explainer baselines. It does not measure whether features overlap within limited dimensions or why neurons are polysemantic. It also does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units of the model. The DLA case studies compare GAE's adapted decoder with the unadapted (Fixed) one. Any change in attribution is caused by the authors' own method, not by a property of the model's representation. The one finding about dictionaries themselves is geometric misalignment of ID-trained dictionaries under shift. It is a subspace-overlap measure, not a test of feature identity or stability, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that OOD faithfulness degradation in dictionary explainers has a geometric cause: the decoder subspace drifts from the OOD-active subspace, and this gap bounds excess projection loss. Their closed-form GAE realigns and refits the decoder without gradients, matching or beating training-based baselines, including retraining, in most settings. They note that preserving activations does not guarantee unchanged semantics or causal effects.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a geometric dictionary-adaptation procedure; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method or its measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Decoder adaptation changes feature DLA and class-specificity even when feature IDs and activations are held fixed; in the HaluEval mechanism ablation, Step 1-Only and Step 2-Only produce different feature-faithfulness outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: ID-trained SAE and transcoder decoder subspaces align with the ID-active subspace but misalign with the OOD-active subspace under domain and adversarial shift. The OOD-side gap is 1.35–1.69× the ID-side gap for transcoders and 1.11–1.12× for SAEs (Table 6). Fixed-explainer faithfulness under OOD falls below what adaptation recovers (Tables 2–3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionaries trained in-distribution do not remain aligned with the subspace a model actively uses under distribution shift. This bears on the distribution-stability of dictionary features, measured geometrically rather than as feature identity.

record.problems: The V5-related evidence is limited to selected features and prompts in GPT-2 Small, and compares deliberately adapted explainer decoders rather than testing whether SAE features are complete or canonical units of the target model. Main experimental comparisons generally have no error bars; Table 11 reports paired-bootstrap intervals.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the claim versions not tested. GAE faithfulness tables, geometric-gap results, and other experiments concern explainer adaptation or OOD projection rather than the listed superposition and feature-unit claims.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transition and geometry. The toy MLP here tests explainer subspace drift only.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recoverable by SAEs. SAEs are used, not evaluated for this.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features. Only adapted-vs-fixed decoder attributions and subspace drift are measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5 classification and V5 labels are reversed to T4 with no labels. All five rows contrast the authors' own adapted decoder with the unadapted one, so the attribution changes are artefacts of the intervention, not evidence about SAE features as model units. R5 additionally uses features selected by GAE causal effect. The only potentially relevant finding, explainer subspace drift under shift, is recorded in fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap of sparse features, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or whether sparse features are recovered as model features by dictionaries.

The study evaluates selected feature interpretations under decoder adaptation, not completeness or canonicality of SAE features generally, nor their stability across models and ordinary changes in inputs or training.
Whether represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small (Transcoder)
rows.operation_detail: Compared Fixed and GAE direct logit attribution (DLA) for the same three selected features with identical activations on a prompt predicting “American”.

conditions.value: same top-3 feature IDs and activations

rows.measure: Class-specificity summed over the three features, measured as nationality-token DLA relative to non-nationality controls.
rows.note: The reported class-specificity changes sign after decoder adaptation, despite identical feature activations; this concerns the adapted explainer decoder, not a change to the target model.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method (GAE decoder) with the Fixed decoder on one selected prompt. The sign flip in class-specificity is produced by the authors' adaptation, so it does not show whether SAE features are canonical or stable units of the model. This is a method comparison, not a measurement for V5.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small (Transcoder)
rows.operation_detail: Compared class-specific DLA for the same three selected features under Fixed, Step 1-Only, and GAE.

conditions.value: selected using Fixed on a disjoint ID split and held fixed across methods

rows.measure: Mean class-specific DLA; sign retention and Fixed–GAE DLA correlation across feature–prompt pairs.
rows.value: Step 1-Only mean DLA: 1.24; GAE mean DLA: 1.39; sign retention: 94.4%; Fixed–GAE correlation: 0.89
rows.uncertainty: 95% paired-bootstrap CI for mean GAE-minus-Fixed DLA difference: [0.03, 0.13]
rows.note: The paper says these results support concept-selective retention for the evaluated features and prompts, not universal semantic or causal invariance.
rows.check: Concept-retention numbers compare Fixed, Step 1-Only and GAE decoders, i.e. the study's own method against variants and the baseline. They measure whether GAE preserves attributions, not whether dictionary features are the model's units.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small (Transcoder)
rows.operation_detail: Compared DLA for the same three selected features with identical activations under Fixed and GAE.

conditions.value: HaluEval prompt predicting a male first name (“Henry”)

rows.note: The same features retain a positive class-specific score, but the attribution magnitude increases substantially after decoder adaptation.
